content.intro: This lesson focuses on your first angular application inside Introduction to Angular. Begin with the syllabus anchor “Creating a starter project”, name the data or UI behavior involved, and then verify the result with a focused example. The goal is to make one clear engineering decision rather than memorize an isolated API.
content.why_it_matters: Your First Angular Application helps keep Angular features understandable as the application grows. A small explicit pattern is easier to reuse, test and review than scattered UI-specific logic.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Create or use a disposable Angular CLI workspace with a compatible Angular/Node/TypeScript version. Put the snippet in the matching component, template, stylesheet or project configuration; satisfy imports and providers from the surrounding lesson context. content_blocks.title: Engineering note
content_blocks.text: Execution note: this CodeLeaf course presents Angular and TypeScript snippets as static teaching material. The browser playground does not compile Angular TypeScript; run examples in a locally generated Angular workspace and verify them with the matching CLI, tests and browser.

content.task: Apply your first angular application to a small feature in a disposable Angular learning project. Demonstrate at least one supplied subtopic (Creating a starter project), record the expected UI or console result, and include one test, failure case or version note.
task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates “Creating a starter project” in the context of Your First Angular Application.
The learner explains the expected result and includes an empty, invalid or failure case where appropriate.
Verification evidence matches the actual environment; a static CodeLeaf snippet is not described as a successfully executed Angular build.
hints: Start with the syllabus item “Creating a starter project” and write down the expected behavior before changing code.
Keep the example small; include only dependencies, inputs, providers and state that the example actually needs.
Reproduce the intended behavior in a pinned local Angular workspace and inspect both normal and failure paths.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without checking its surrounding context.
common_mistakes.why: Angular examples can depend on imports, providers, template context or a particular framework version.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the run instructions and validate against the exact generated workspace.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating an attractive UI result as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Accessibility, boundary cases, failures and server-side rules may not be visible in the happy path.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a focused assertion and test at least one realistic failure state.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming client code guarantees authorization or validates all external data.
common_mistakes.why: Browser code is controlled by the client and can receive unexpected network responses.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate external values and enforce protected business rules on the backend.
